## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the general operation, care, and policies governing
the ThermoFisher Delta V Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometer (IRMS) and its
four front-end peripherals in the Oxtoby Environmental Isotope Lab. It
is the single instrument-level reference for all IRMS work. Individual
application SOPs (e.g., [SOP-L414](SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd) for soil
CN analysis, [SOP-L415](SOP-L415-carbonate-gasbench-irms.qmd) for
carbonate isotopes) build on this SOP and should be read in conjunction
with it.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** The Delta V IRMS and all peripherals (ConFlo IV,
  Flash IRMS EA, TC/EA, GasBench II) in the Oxtoby Isotope Lab,
  SGM Rm 135, Pomona College.
- **Does not apply to:** Application-specific sample preparation, data
  reduction, or QC criteria. See the relevant application SOP.
- **Location:** David W. and Claire B. Oxtoby Environmental Isotope Lab
  (SGM Rm 135). Sample preparation: wet lab (SGM Rm 133).


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role               | Responsibility                                           |
|:-------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI             | Approve methods, authorize access, oversee training      |
| Lab Manager (0.5 FTE) | Prepare/verify instrument methods; train users; maintain reactors and columns |
| Super-User         | Supervise trainees; perform minor maintenance (gas replacement, reactor exchange, needle exchange, PAL programming) |
| Certified User     | Prepare samples, build sequences, run analyses independently |
| Student Researcher | Sample weighing, data reduction, sequence creation (no unsupervised runs) |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Pressurized gases:** H~2~, O~2~, CO, CO~2~, SO~2~, He, N~2~.
  Several are reactive or toxic. Always verify cylinder pressures before
  starting work.
- **Hot surfaces:** Flash EA reactors, TC/EA pyrolysis tube (~1450 °C),
  and ash fingers. Risk of burns during handling.
- **Chemical reagents:** 100% phosphoric acid (GasBench carbonate
  method), chromium oxide, silvered cobaltous/cobaltic oxide, tungsten
  oxide, vanadium pentoxide, quartz wool, and other oxidants/reductants
  used in reactor packing.
- **Sharps:** Syringes, needles, and other pointed tools (GasBench,
  TC/EA).
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat (bring your own; limited loaners available)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (various sizes in the lab; donations welcome)

### Emergency Procedures

Follow the procedures in
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd). Contact the
lab manager or Dr. Marc Los Huertos immediately for gas leaks, spills,
injuries, or instrument malfunctions.

## 6. User Certification

### 6.1 User Categories

Student Researcher
: May conduct sample weighing, sequence creation, and data reduction.
  May not operate the IRMS without direct supervision.

User
: A student, staff, or faculty member certified to prepare samples and
  run the IRMS without supervision.

Super-User
: A staff or faculty member qualified to run the IRMS and perform minor
  maintenance.

### 6.2 Training Pathway

Since the lab is managed by a half-time manager, users must be able to
operate the instruments independently. Training ensures users are both
qualified and *confident*.

**Estimated time:** Approximately 6 hours of observation, supervised
practice, and minimally supervised runs (not including reading time).
Training for a single peripheral is shorter than training across all
peripherals.

**Steps to certification:**

1. Complete the required reading (this SOP plus the relevant application
   SOP).
2. Complete [SOP-L01 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L01-laboratory-safety.qmd).
3. Observe one or more experienced users operate the IRMS and the
   peripheral(s) you will use.
4. Conduct supervised practice runs.
5. Complete a start-to-finish analysis. The lab technician or a
   designated Super-User will determine whether the trainee is ready
   for independent use.


## 7. Laboratory Policies

### 7.1 Not a Service Lab

The Oxtoby Laboratory is not a service lab. The manager ensures methods
are working properly but will not prepare samples, create sequences,
oversee runs, or conduct data reduction. Users are responsible for all
of these tasks.

### 7.2 Scheduling and Access

Instrument time is first-come, first-served, with PI priority. **Expect
delays** if you are scheduled immediately after another user; unforeseen
events happen. Lab access is generally 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM unless the
technician or Dr. Los Huertos is in the department. Contact the
technician
([kyle.mccarty@pomona.edu](mailto:kyle.mccarty@pomona.edu)) to schedule
time or arrange access.

### 7.3 Consumables (In-Kind Payment Model)

There is no per-sample cost, but users are expected to replenish
consumables and gases relative to their use. You are welcome to bring
your own consumables (capsules, cell wells, weighing paper, gloves,
standards, reagents, vials, caps, septa, needles, syringes, reactor
tubes, etc.).

### 7.4 Housekeeping

- Clean up after yourself: Kimwipes, weighing papers, waste.
- Organize your samples and personal items whether you are in or out of
  the lab.
- Push in your chairs. Keep the lab tidy and free of obstructions.


## 8. Instrument Overview

### 8.1 How Gas Source IRMS Works

Isotope ratio mass spectrometers measure small differences in the
abundances of isotopes, usually of the lighter elements. The Delta V can
measure $^{2}$H/$^{1}$H, $^{13}$C/$^{12}$C, $^{15}$N/$^{14}$N,
$^{18}$O/$^{16}$O, and $^{34}$S/$^{32}$S.

Before isotope ratios can be determined, samples are converted into
simple gases: H~2~, CO, N~2~, CO~2~, or SO~2~. The IRMS separates
ions by their mass-to-charge ratio (m/z). It cannot distinguish
between molecular species of the same m/z (e.g., N~2~ and CO both
appear at m/z 28), so proper sample conversion and chromatographic
separation are essential. Measured ratios are compared to reference
gases and verified against certified standards to produce delta
($\delta$) values.

### 8.2 Continuous Flow vs. Dual Inlet

The Oxtoby Lab uses a continuous-flow (CF-IRMS) configuration. One or
more peripherals are coupled to the IRMS through the ConFlo IV
interface. Dual-inlet IRMS (DI-IRMS) is roughly 10 times more precise
but requires more sample preparation, larger sample sizes, and has lower
throughput. The lab does not currently have a dual-inlet system.

### 8.3 The Four Peripherals

#### ConFlo IV

The hub connecting all peripherals, reference gases, and the IRMS. It
dilutes sample and reference gas streams so that signal intensities fall
within the working range of the mass spectrometer. All gas lines
(carrier, reference, and sample) pass through the ConFlo.

#### Flash IRMS EA (Elemental Analyzer)

Combusts solid samples in an oxygen-enriched helium stream to produce
N~2~, CO~2~, and (optionally) SO~2~. Gases are separated on a packed
chromatographic column and carried to the IRMS via the ConFlo IV.
Available configurations:

- **NC dual reactor:** For $\delta^{13}$C and $\delta^{15}$N.
- **NCS single reactor:** Adds $\delta^{34}$S using a dedicated reactor,
  Sulfinert column, and SO~2~ reference gas with heated regulator/foil.

The autosampler holds three carousels of 32 wells each (94 positions
total).

#### TC/EA (Thermal Conversion/Elemental Analyzer)

Uses high-temperature pyrolysis (~1450 °C) instead of combustion to
convert samples into H~2~ and CO for $\delta^{2}$H and $\delta^{18}$O
analysis. Accepts solid samples in silver capsules (up to 6 mm diameter)
or liquid injections. Consumes substantially more helium than the
Flash EA (no helium-saving feature).

#### GasBench II

A low-flow peripheral that samples headspace gas from sealed vials
(usually via a PAL autosampler), conditions it (water removal, gas
chromatographic separation), and transports it to the IRMS. Applications
include:

- Carbonate $\delta^{13}$C and $\delta^{18}$O (phosphoric acid
  digestion)
- Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC)
- Breath gas analysis
- CO~2~ at atmospheric concentrations
- Water equilibration for $\delta^{18}$O and $\delta^{2}$H

Each vial is sampled multiple times (typically 11 injections), so
per-sample analysis times are longer than you might initially expect.
The GasBench has the added complexity of PAL autosampler programming
for vial flushing, which cannot run simultaneously with IRMS analysis.


## 9. Reference and Carrier Gases

### 9.1 Tank Farm 1 (West Wall, North)

| Gas                    | Role              | Pressure Requirements                |
|:-----------------------|:------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| Helium (He)            | Carrier gas       | Tank >500 psi, regulated at 50 psi   |
| Nitrogen (N~2~)        | Reference gas     | Per method specification             |
| Carbon dioxide (CO~2~) | Reference gas     | Per method specification             |
| Oxygen (O~2~)          | Combustion gas    | Flash EA only                        |

### 9.2 Tank Farm 2 (West Wall, South)

| Gas                         | Role / Notes          |
|:----------------------------|:----------------------|
| Hydrogen (H~2~)             | Reference gas         |
| Carbon monoxide (CO)        | Reference gas         |
| H~2~/He mix                 | TC/EA carrier         |
| H~2~/CO~2~ mix              | GasBench              |
| Sulfur dioxide (SO~2~)      | Reference gas (NCS)   |

::: {.callout-important}
Always verify that you have enough carrier and reference gas for the
full duration of your run **before** starting. Running out of gas
mid-sequence can damage the source and waste an entire batch of samples.
:::

## 11. Instrument Startup and Shutdown

### 11.1 Starting from a Cold State

If the IRMS has been completely powered down:

1. Verify all gas valves are open and compressed air is connected.
2. Confirm the needle valve is closed.
3. Turn on the system with the MAIN SWITCH.
4. Power on the computer and launch Isodat.
5. Switch on pumps at the Control Panel.
6. In the MS State panel, switch on all heaters required for your
   analysis.
7. In the Accessories toolbar of Isodat, access the ion source
   settings.
8. Allow 24--48 hours for the instrument to stabilize before running
   analyses.

### 11.2 Starting from Standby

If the IRMS has been in standby (source on, peripherals off):

1. Verify gas pressures (see @sec-gas-checks).
2. Power on the peripheral you will use (Flash EA, TC/EA, or
   GasBench II).
3. Initialize the peripheral's temperature ramp and purge cycle.
4. Proceed to pre-analysis checks (@sec-pre-analysis).

### 11.3 Shutdown

1. Confirm the sequence has completed successfully in Isodat.
2. Follow the peripheral-specific shutdown procedure (contact the lab
   manager if unsure).
3. If the instrument will be idle for more than a few days, consult the
   lab manager about placing it in standby or full shutdown.
4. Log your gas usage and any issues in the lab logbook.


## 12. Gas Checks {#sec-gas-checks}

Before every session, verify:

- He tank pressure >500 psi, regulated at 50 psi.
- Sufficient reference gas for the planned run duration.
- O~2~ supply (Flash EA sessions).
- Gas flows within specification for your method (check Isodat
  Instrument Monitor).


## 13. Pre-Analysis Checks {#sec-pre-analysis}

### 13.1 Instrument Status

- No red or yellow warning lights on the IRMS front panel.
- Vacuum gauge within acceptable range.
- High voltage (HV), box, and trap values reading back normally in
  Isodat.

### 13.2 Purge, Bake-Out, and Temperature Ramp

1. Purge atmospheric gases from the system.
2. Perform a column bake-out if the instrument has been idle.
3. Initialize the temperature ramp for the relevant reactor (Flash EA
   combustion reactor, TC/EA pyrolysis tube, or GasBench transfer
   line).

### 13.3 Background Checks

Verify residual gas backgrounds in the ion source. Elevated backgrounds
indicate leaks or contamination:

| m/z | Species        | Possible Cause                         |
|:---:|:---------------|:---------------------------------------|
| 2   | He$^{2+}$      | High He pressure or source tuning      |
| 18  | H~2~O$^{+}$    | Moisture leak or insufficient bake-out |
| 28  | N~2~$^{+}$     | Air leak                               |
| 40  | Ar$^{+}$       | Air leak                               |
| 44  | CO~2~$^{+}$    | Residual CO~2~ or combustion byproduct |

### 13.4 Zero-Enrichment (On/Off) Tests

Perform reference gas on/off tests to verify the IRMS is within
specification. Each cycle takes approximately 10 minutes. You will
almost always need multiple cycles, and the instrument can drift out of
specification if it has been idle.

::: {.callout-caution}
Do not skip or rush this step. Proceeding with out-of-spec on/off tests
produces unreliable data.
:::

### 13.5 H~3~$^{+}$ Factor ($\delta^{2}$H Only)

If your analysis includes $\delta^{2}$H, determine the H~3~$^{+}$
factor before proceeding (~8 minutes).

### 13.6 Blank Determination (Solid Samples)

Run several blank capsules (empty, crimped) to quantify background
contribution. Blank peak areas should be negligible relative to sample
peaks.


## 14. Tuning

For continuous-flow analysis, tune the IRMS for **linearity** (consistent
ion ratios across a range of signal intensities), not maximum
sensitivity. Tuning for linearity minimizes the dependence of measured
$\delta$ values on peak amplitude, which is critical because sample
sizes (and therefore peak sizes) vary.


## 15. Isodat Software Basics

### 15.1 Creating a Sequence

1. Open the Acquisition module and create a new sequence (click the
   sequence icon).
2. Define the number of sample positions.
3. Select the appropriate method. If no suitable method exists, contact
   the lab manager.
4. Verify that **Peak Center** has a green check mark.
5. Enter identifiers in the "Identifier 1" column.
6. Use the autofill function to assign the method to all rows.

### 15.2 File Naming Convention

Save sequences and data files as:

`YYYYMMDD_Project_SequenceID_Username.seq`

### 15.3 Running a Sequence

1. Load samples into the autosampler.
2. Verify that physical positions match the Isodat sequence.
3. Click **Start** and enter the file name.

### 15.4 Exporting Data

Export completed results as CSV for data reduction. Include at minimum:
sample identifier, peak areas for each mass channel, raw $\delta$ values
vs. the reference gas, and signal amplitudes.


## 16. Time Management

Using the IRMS takes a great deal of time. Set aside multiple,
relatively uninterrupted days.

### 16.1 Common Time Sinks

- Bake-out and stabilization (hours to overnight).
- Background and on/off checks (budget at least 1--2 hours; variable).
- Sample weighing (~1--2 minutes per capsule for beginners).
- The analytical run itself (see approximate times below).
- Data reduction (budget a full session).

### 16.2 Approximate Per-Sample Run Times

#### Flash EA

| Analysis              | Time per Sample (approx.) |
|:----------------------|:-------------------------:|
| $\delta^{15}$N only   | ~4--5 min                 |
| $\delta^{13}$C only   | ~5--6 min                 |
| NC dual method        | ~7--8 min                 |
| NCS triple analysis   | ~11--12 min               |

#### GasBench II

| Analysis                        | Time per Sample (approx.) |
|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------:|
| Carbonates (CO~2~\_630 method)  | ~11--12 min               |

The GasBench samples each vial 11 times, which extends per-sample time.
The PAL autosampler flushing stage cannot run concurrently with IRMS
analysis, so plan accordingly.

#### TC/EA

| Analysis                   | Time per Sample (approx.) |
|:---------------------------|:-------------------------:|
| $\delta^{2}$H only         | ~4--5 min                 |
| $\delta^{18}$O only        | TBD                       |
| Dual ($^{2}$H + $^{18}$O) | ~7 min                    |

All times include approximately one additional minute for peak centering
and magnet switching.

## 18. Troubleshooting

| Symptom                              | Possible Cause / Action                       |
|:-------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| High m/z 28 background               | Air leak; check fittings and reactor seals    |
| High m/z 18 background               | Moisture; extend bake-out time                |
| High m/z 40 background               | Air leak (Ar); check fittings                 |
| Poor standard reproducibility        | Capsule sealing; exhausted reactor            |
| No peaks in chromatogram            | Gas flow interrupted; check He supply          |
| Sequence stops mid-run              | Autosampler jam; check carousel alignment      |
| On/off tests fail repeatedly         | Source needs tuning or maintenance             |
| Red/yellow lights on IRMS panel      | Check Isodat error log; contact lab manager   |

If you cannot resolve an issue, **stop the run** and contact the lab
manager. Do not attempt reactor replacement or major maintenance unless
you are a certified Super-User.


## 19. Definitions

ConFlo IV
: Interface hub connecting peripherals, reference gases, and the IRMS.
  Handles gas dilution.

Delta V IRMS
: The ThermoFisher Delta V Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometer.

Flash IRMS EA
: Elemental analyzer peripheral. Combusts samples to produce N~2~,
  CO~2~, and (optionally) SO~2~.

GasBench II
: Low-flow peripheral for headspace gas sampling from sealed vials.

H~3~$^{+}$ Factor
: Correction for H~3~$^{+}$ ions formed in the source, which interfere
  with HD$^{+}$ at m/z 3 during $\delta^{2}$H analysis.

Linearity
: The relationship between measured $\delta$ and signal amplitude. A
  well-tuned instrument shows minimal dependence.

Super-User
: Staff or faculty certified for operation and minor maintenance.

TC/EA
: Thermal Conversion/Elemental Analyzer. Pyrolysis at ~1450 °C produces
  H~2~ and CO.

User
: Certified individual who may operate the IRMS independently.

Zero-Enrichment Test
: Reference gas on/off pulses verifying the IRMS produces consistent
  $\delta$ values.

## 22. Training Record

Before using the IRMS independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
3. Read the application SOP for the peripheral(s) they will use
4. Observe at least one complete analysis session by an experienced user
5. Complete supervised practice runs
6. Demonstrate a start-to-finish analysis to the satisfaction of the
   lab technician or a Super-User
7. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
